<!-- Source: README.md -->

# @codenhub/theme

Zero-dependency browser theme preference, persistence, DOM, and token manager.

## Installation

```sh
pnpm add @codenhub/theme
```

## Usage

```ts
import { createTheme } from "@codenhub/theme";

const theme = createTheme().init();

button.addEventListener("click", theme.toggle);
theme.subscribe(({ name }) => console.log(`theme is now ${name}`));

// Inline this string in a blocking <head> script to apply the theme before the first paint:
const script = theme.getPrePaintScript();

// Remove media-query/storage listeners and subscribers on teardown.
theme.destroy({ revertDom: true });
```

## Documentation

- [Documentation overview](docs/index.md)
- [Tokens, persistence, and cross-tab sync](docs/tokens-and-persistence.md)
- [SSR, pre-paint, and Tailwind](docs/ssr-and-pre-paint.md)
- [API reference](docs/reference/index.md)

## Requirements

- Browser integration uses `document.documentElement`, `localStorage`, `matchMedia`, `storage` events, and `CustomEvent`.
- SSR is supported by skipping unavailable browser work and using the configured default theme.
- Consumers provide CSS selectors, variables, and visual tokens, and inline the script from `getPrePaintScript()` to prevent a theme flash.

## Notes

Construction validates theme names, mappings, attributes, classes, and token schemas and throws on invalid configuration. Storage failures are reported to the console and treated as unavailable storage.

Licensed under Apache-2.0.

<!-- Source: docs/index.md -->

# Manage Browser Themes

`@codenhub/theme` owns one thing for a browser application: deciding which theme is active, keeping it in sync with `localStorage` and the OS `prefers-color-scheme` setting, and reflecting it onto the DOM as an attribute, a class, a `color-scheme`, and CSS custom properties. It fits applications that want one place to own that decision instead of scattering `matchMedia` listeners and `localStorage` reads across the codebase, while keeping selectors, visual design, and CSS entirely in application code.

## Setup

### Installation

```sh
pnpm add @codenhub/theme
```

### Quick start

```ts
import { createTheme } from "@codenhub/theme";

const theme = createTheme().init();

button.addEventListener("click", theme.toggle);
```

`createTheme()` with no arguments configures the built-in `light` and `dark` themes. `init()` resolves the theme to apply — a stored preference if one is valid, otherwise the OS preference — and applies it to `document.documentElement`. Every method is bound to its manager, so `theme.toggle` and `theme.subscribe` can be passed as callbacks directly. Call `destroy()` when the manager's owner is torn down, such as in a framework component's cleanup hook; it stops listening but leaves the DOM and stored preference as they were unless told otherwise (see [SSR, pre-paint, and Tailwind](docs/ssr-and-pre-paint.md)).

### Reading state

| Member             | Value                                                                               |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `theme.name`       | Active theme name.                                                                  |
| `theme.get()`      | Active theme — `name`, `colorScheme`, `tokens`, `pairedTheme` — as a frozen object. |
| `theme.preference` | Explicit stored preference, or `null` while the theme follows the OS.               |
| `theme.system`     | Theme the OS preference maps to right now.                                          |

`get()` returns the same object until the next change, so it works directly as a store snapshot. In React:

```ts
const active = useSyncExternalStore(theme.subscribe, theme.get, theme.get);
```

### Configuration

Most applications configure their themes and a `tokenSchema` up front:

```ts
import { createTheme } from "@codenhub/theme";

const theme = createTheme({
  themes: {
    light: { colorScheme: "light", tokens: { primary: "#171717" } },
    dark: { colorScheme: "dark", tokens: { primary: "#f9fafb" } },
    dim: { colorScheme: "dark", pairedTheme: "light" },
  },
  tokenSchema: { primary: "--color-primary" },
  storageKey: "app-theme-preference",
  darkClass: true,
}).init();

theme.set("dim");
```

`themes` is keyed by theme name and replaces the built-in list entirely — include `light` and `dark`, or set `defaultTheme` and `systemTheme` to names you do define. Theme names are inferred from its keys, so `defaultTheme`, `systemTheme`, `pairedTheme`, and `set()` accept only configured names at compile time. `tokenSchema` maps the typed token names used in `tokens` to the CSS custom property each one writes to `document.documentElement`. See [Tokens, persistence, and cross-tab sync](docs/tokens-and-persistence.md) for how token values are resolved and stored, and [SSR, pre-paint, and Tailwind](docs/ssr-and-pre-paint.md) for flash-of-unstyled-content prevention, `darkClass`, and `className`.

Construction validates every option and throws on invalid configuration: a `themes` value that is not an object, an empty theme name, a `defaultTheme`, `systemTheme`, or `pairedTheme` name that is not in `themes`, an invalid `colorScheme`, theme tokens outside `tokenSchema`, or a theme name that cannot form the default `theme-<name>` class.

An option set to `undefined` uses its default, exactly as an omitted one does. The option types accept `undefined`, so a wrapper that forwards an unset option, such as `storageKey: props.storageKey`, gets the default instead of a construction error. Rejecting `undefined` was the behavior before 0.2.0; it was dropped because it failed at runtime on code the types accept.

## Requirements

- Browser integration uses `document.documentElement`, `localStorage`, `matchMedia`, `storage` events, and `CustomEvent`. Every one of these is read defensively: an unavailable or throwing API is treated as absent rather than crashing the caller.
- SSR is supported by skipping unavailable browser work and using the configured `defaultTheme`. The package cannot produce server HTML attributes or prevent a flash on its own — see [SSR, pre-paint, and Tailwind](docs/ssr-and-pre-paint.md).
- Consumers provide CSS selectors, variables, and visual tokens. The package only ever writes an attribute, optional classes, `color-scheme`, and CSS custom properties — it ships no CSS or token values.

## Next steps

- [Tokens, persistence, and cross-tab sync](docs/tokens-and-persistence.md): How token values are resolved, how preferences persist to `localStorage` and sync across tabs, and how to react to changes.
- [SSR, pre-paint, and Tailwind](docs/ssr-and-pre-paint.md): Preventing a flash of unstyled content before hydration, server-rendering considerations, and the classes the package applies.
- [API reference](docs/reference/index.md): Every exported function, type, and interface member with its full signature.

<!-- Source: docs/ssr-and-pre-paint.md -->

# SSR, Pre-Paint, and Tailwind

## Preventing a flash of unstyled content

A client-side `init()` call runs after the page has already painted once, which is visible as a flash from the default theme to the resolved one. `getPrePaintScript()` returns a synchronous, minified inline IIFE string that repeats the same stored-preference-then-system-preference resolution and applies the configured attribute, `color-scheme`, classes, and static tokens before the browser paints:

```ts
import { createTheme } from "@codenhub/theme";

import { themeOptions } from "./theme-options";

const script = createTheme(themeOptions).getPrePaintScript();
```

`createTheme()` is safe to call on the server, so one options module can build the script there and the manager in the browser, keeping the two in agreement. Inject the returned string into a blocking `<script>` in the document `<head>`, before any stylesheet or content that depends on the theme:

```html
<head>
  <script>
    /* inline the string returned by getPrePaintScript() here */
  </script>
</head>
```

The script handles storage and `matchMedia` failures the same way `init()` does: blocked storage still applies the system theme, and a missing `matchMedia` applies `defaultTheme`. It removes the classes of other configured themes, so a class rendered by the server is replaced rather than joined. It serializes only **static** tokens from each theme's `tokens`; runtime overrides from `setTokens()` exist only in the running page and cannot be part of a script that runs before any application code.

## Server-side rendering

Without browser APIs, `Theme` methods skip storage reads/writes, DOM updates, and listener registration; `theme.system` falls back to `defaultTheme`. Every member remains safe to use during SSR — nothing throws for a missing `window`, `document`, or `localStorage` — but the package cannot produce server-rendered HTML attributes on its own. To avoid a flash on a server-rendered page, either:

- Render the server markup with the same attribute/class the pre-paint script would apply (requiring the server to read the same cookie or header a real theme service would use), or
- Rely on the pre-paint script above to correct the DOM before first paint, accepting that server-rendered markup itself does not carry theme state.

Keep any server-side resolution logic — stored names, system mapping, storage key, attribute, classes, color scheme — aligned with the options passed to `createTheme()`; a mismatch reintroduces the flash it exists to prevent.

## Tailwind's `dark` class

Set `darkClass: true` to add a `dark` class to `document.documentElement` while a theme whose `colorScheme` is `"dark"` is active, as Tailwind CSS's class-based `dark:` variant expects. This is independent of `className` (below) — a Tailwind app commonly wants both the `dark` class and, when `className` is left at its default, a `theme-<name>` class for custom per-theme CSS.

## Classes and cleanup

`className` controls the class applied to `document.documentElement` alongside the attribute: `true` (the default) applies `theme-<name>`, `false` applies no class, and a `ThemeClassResolver` function receives the theme with its static tokens and returns one custom class token. A resolver runs once per theme, on first use rather than at construction, and the operation that triggered it throws if it returns an empty or whitespace-containing string.

`destroy(options?)` removes the media-query and storage listeners and clears in-process subscribers and runtime tokens, leaving the instance safe to `init()` again. By default it does **not** touch the DOM or stored preference. Pass `{ revertDom: true }` to also remove the configured attribute, classes, `color-scheme`, and CSS custom properties from `document.documentElement` — useful when unmounting a scoped theme manager that should leave no trace, such as in a component test or a preview pane.

<!-- Source: docs/tokens-and-persistence.md -->

# Tokens, Persistence, and Cross-Tab Sync

## Token resolution

`tokenSchema` maps typed token names to the CSS custom property each one writes, such as `{ primary: "--color-primary" }`. Each token can come from three sources, in this priority order (last wins):

1. **Computed style** — the value CSS gives the property on `document.documentElement`, for a token not defined in JS.
2. **Theme static tokens** — values set on the active theme's `tokens`.
3. **Runtime overrides** — values passed to `setTokens()`.

`get().tokens` holds the JS sources, 2 and 3, and never reads the DOM. `readTokens()` adds the computed values of the remaining tokens at the time of the call:

```ts
const theme = createTheme({
  themes: {
    light: { colorScheme: "light", tokens: { accent: "#ff6600" } },
    dark: { colorScheme: "dark" },
  },
  tokenSchema: { accent: "--color-accent", surface: "--color-surface" },
}).init();

theme.setTokens({ accent: "#00c853" }); // runtime override wins over the static "#ff6600"
theme.get().tokens; // { accent: "#00c853" }
theme.readTokens(); // { accent: "#00c853", surface: "<computed --color-surface>" }
```

Reading computed values can force a synchronous layout, so prefer `get().tokens` when tokens defined only in CSS are not needed. `readTokens()` skips the read when every token is known in JS.

Runtime overrides apply to every theme and persist across theme changes until `setTokens()` replaces them — pass `{}` to remove them. They are not stored, so they last until the page unloads or `destroy()` runs, and they are not part of the pre-paint script. Passing a token key that is not in `tokenSchema` throws.

## Persistence

An explicit preference set through `set()` or `toggle()` is written to `localStorage` under `storageKey` (default `"app-theme-preference"`). `theme.preference` returns that value when it names a configured theme, or `null` when it is unset, invalid, or storage is unavailable (for example during SSR). `clearPreference()` removes the stored value and applies `theme.system`, the theme the OS preference currently maps to.

Storage reads, writes, and removals that throw — a full quota, a disabled storage API, a private-browsing restriction — are logged with `console.error` and treated the same as unavailable storage; they never throw out of `Theme` methods.

## Cross-tab sync

Every tab running `createTheme().init()` against the same `storageKey` stays in sync: when another tab sets, clears, or invalidates the stored preference — including through `localStorage.clear()` — each tab re-resolves its theme from storage and the OS preference and notifies with `source: "storage"`. A tab with its own runtime token overrides keeps them; only the active theme changes.

The OS `prefers-color-scheme` media query applies automatically only while no valid stored preference exists. Once a tab (or a previous session) has stored an explicit preference, later system-preference changes are ignored until `clearPreference()` runs.

## Reacting to changes

`subscribe(listener)` registers a callback invoked after every applied change and returns an unsubscribe function:

```ts
const unsubscribe = theme.subscribe(({ name, source }) => {
  console.log(`theme is now "${name}" (${source})`);
});
```

`source` names what caused the change: the method that ran (`"init"`, `"set"`, `"toggle"`, `"clearPreference"`, `"setTokens"`), `"system"` for an OS color-scheme change, or `"storage"` for a change made in another tab. Code that mirrors the preference elsewhere, such as to a user profile, should act on `"set"`, `"toggle"`, and `"clearPreference"` only, so that every open tab does not repeat the same write.

A subscriber that throws is logged and does not stop other subscribers from running. Browsers also receive a `window` `CustomEvent` named by the exported `THEME_CHANGE_EVENT` constant (`"themechange"`) carrying the same detail, for code that has no access to the manager. The event does not identify which manager sent it, so use `subscribe()` when a page runs more than one.

<!-- Source: docs/changelog/0.2.0.md -->

# 0.2.0

## Added

- Theme names are inferred from the keys of `themes`, so `defaultTheme`, `systemTheme`, `pairedTheme`, and `set()` reject unconfigured names at compile time.
- `theme.name`, `theme.preference`, and `theme.system` getters read the active name, the stored preference, and the theme the OS preference maps to.
- `setTokens(tokens)` replaces the runtime token overrides; pass `{}` to remove them. Changes it makes report `source: "setTokens"`.
- `readTokens()` returns every token, completed with computed CSS values at the time of the call.
- Changes made in another tab report `source: "storage"`, so code that mirrors the preference elsewhere can tell them from local changes.

## Changed

- `themes` is an object keyed by theme name instead of an array: `{ light: { colorScheme: "light" } }` replaces `[{ name: "light", colorScheme: "light" }]`.
- Methods are bound to their manager, so `theme.toggle` and `theme.subscribe` can be passed as callbacks directly.
- `get()` returns the same frozen object until the next change and never reads the DOM, so it can serve as a store snapshot such as `useSyncExternalStore(theme.subscribe, theme.get)`. Its `tokens` holds static and runtime tokens only; call `readTokens()` for tokens defined only in CSS.
- `isTailwindCss` is renamed `darkClass`, and `shouldApplyClass` is renamed `className`.
- `Theme`, `ThemeOptions`, and the other generic types take the theme name union as their first type parameter, before the token schema.
- When another tab sets, clears, or invalidates the preference, every tab re-resolves its theme and notifies, even when the active theme stays the same, so a settings screen sees the preference change.
- Listener errors are logged as `[theme] Error in theme change listener:`, matching the package's other messages.

## Removed

- The standalone `getPrePaintScript(options)` export. Use `createTheme(options).getPrePaintScript()`, which is safe to call on the server.
- The `LIGHT_THEME` and `DARK_THEME` exports; the built-in themes are the default `themes` value.
- `getStored()`, `getSystem()`, and `get({ skipComputed })`; use `preference`, `system`, and `get()` with `readTokens()`.
- The `tokens` parameter of `init()`, `set()`, and `toggle()`; use `setTokens()`.

## Fixed

- Calling `theme.toggle` as an event listener no longer throws, and no longer treats the event as token overrides.
- A snapshot taken before a theme change no longer reports the new theme's computed tokens under the old theme's name.
- The pre-paint script applies the OS theme when `localStorage` access throws, applies `defaultTheme` when `matchMedia` is missing as `init()` does, and replaces a server-rendered theme class instead of adding a second one.
- `localStorage.clear()` in another tab now applies the system theme.
- The pre-paint script falls back as for an unknown name when the stored value is an `Object.prototype` property such as `toString`, and applies a configured theme named `__proto__`. ([#345](https://github.com/codenhub/codenhub/issues/345))
- Invalid options, such as a `defaultTheme` naming an unconfigured theme, throw from `createTheme()` instead of reaching the page through the pre-paint script. ([#364](https://github.com/codenhub/codenhub/issues/364))

## Security

- Theme names, option values, and token values can no longer close the inline `<script>` element or open an HTML comment in the pre-paint script.

# 0.1.2

## Added

- A generated API reference, `docs/reference/index.md`, covering every exported symbol from its TSDoc directly — regenerated on every release instead of hand-maintained separately, so it can't drift out of sync with the source.

## Changed

- Documentation split from one page, `docs/reference.md`, into three focused ones: `docs/index.md` (setup and configuration), `docs/tokens-and-persistence.md` (token resolution, `skipComputed`, persistence, cross-tab sync), and `docs/ssr-and-pre-paint.md` (`getPrePaintScript()`, SSR fallback, Tailwind's `isTailwindCss`, `shouldApplyClass`, `destroy({ revertDom: true })`), plus the generated reference above. Update any link that pointed at `docs/reference.md`.
